solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Concealed weapon revealed in argument between two seconds

indicators.note: between says the argument word sits with one 'second' on each side of it

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a tick is a second, as in 'back in a tick'
words are an argument, as in 'they had words'

explanation.surface: A hidden blade comes out during a row that lasts only a couple of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two seconds' supplies two different words for a second: S on the left and TICK on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordstick is a walking cane with a blade hidden inside it, so a weapon kept out of sight.

clue.text: Bold character in a manuscript held by boy

indicators.note: held by puts the preceding pieces inside the word for boy

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A daring figure turns up in an old document kept by a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical strongman is a byword for boldness and strength, a heroic figure of scripture.

clue.text: Fancy spout round back of urn

indicators.note: round places the speaking word around the letter that follows

parts.note: to spout is to orate, holding forth at length

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word urn

explanation.surface: An ornamental spout fitted around the rear of an urn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spout' looks like a noun for the urn but is a verb meaning to speechify.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborately decorated, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Offensive elegies a bard composed

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters of the three words are put together anew

explanation.surface: Laments written by a poet are found objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Offensive and disagreeable are synonyms, both describing something unpleasant.

clue.text: Pie Italian restaurant served up

indicators.note: served up in a down clue tells us to read the restaurant word from bottom to top

parts.note: trat is a short form of trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: A pie dished out at a trattoria.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry case with a filling, a kind of pie.

clue.text: Assembled coven do act, wickedly

indicators.note: wickedly suggests the letters behave badly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Witches gathered as a coven get up to mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: To convocate is to call together, so convocated means gathered or assembled.

clue.text: Novelist's foreign friends

definitions.meaning: Kingsley or Martin, the father-and-son British novelists, with 's standing for is
French for friends, a foreign word

explanation.definitionFit: The British writers Kingsley and Martin share the surname, and the French plural of ami means friends.

clue.text: Treacle in large quantities — see about tucking in

indicators.note: tucking in puts the turned 'see' word inside the large-quantities word

parts.note: masses are large quantities

indicators.note: about here means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

explanation.surface: Golden syrup by the bucketload; look at people tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is the old exclamation 'lo!', and 'about' turns it round before it goes into the large-quantities word.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark syrup left from sugar refining, called treacle in Britain.

clue.text: Small nuclear weapon demanding attention

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
Trident is the British submarine-launched nuclear missile system

explanation.surface: A compact nuclear device that cannot be ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and harsh, insisting on being noticed.

clue.text: Egg's general character is about right for starter

parts.note: egg is slang for a bomb or mine; with 's for is

indicators.note: about puts the character word around the letter for right

parts.note: tone is the general character or feel of something

explanation.surface: An egg dish whose overall feel suits the opening course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' is old military slang for a mine or bomb, not breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone, the Italian vegetable soup, is commonly served as a first course.

clue.text: Advertising material mostly making indistinct impression

indicators.note: mostly means take the word but not all of it, dropping its last letter

parts.note: a blurb is promotional copy, as on a book jacket

explanation.surface: Most of the promotional copy just leaves a hazy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something seen without clear outlines, a fuzzy perception.

clue.text: Confusion of Cameron's advice on petty criminals in speech?

indicators.note: in speech says the phrase is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: David Cameron, UK Prime Minister, was mocked for urging people to 'hug a hoodie'; the comic extension is to hug a mugger

explanation.surface: A politician's muddled message about street thugs.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron, British Conservative leader, gave a 2006 speech dubbed 'hug a hoodie' (a hoodie being a hooded youth); 'hug a mugger' said quickly gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugger-mugger means disorder or muddle, as well as secrecy.

clue.text: Loss of power taking heart from scandal

indicators.note: taking heart from means the central letter of the scandal word is removed

parts.note: an outrage is a scandal, a shocking affair

explanation.surface: A political scandal loses its punch and its energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A power cut, when electricity supply fails, is called an outage.

clue.text: Foreign Office swore to be single-minded

parts.note: cussed means swore, used bad language

explanation.surface: Diplomats were cursing as they concentrated hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concentrated on one aim is to be single-minded, sharply directed.

clue.text: There's virtue having a gun in game

indicators.note: in puts the weapon pieces inside the game word

parts.note: chess is a board game
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A moral quality is claimed by someone who brings a weapon into play.
explanation.definitionFit: Purity or sexual abstinence is a traditional moral virtue, one of the classical goods.

clue.text: He lent banger, crashing somewhere in East London

indicators.note: crashing suggests the letters collide and are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man loaned an old car which then crashed in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a battered old car (also a sausage).
explanation.definitionFit: Bethnal Green is a district of East London, in the borough of Tower Hamlets.

clue.text: Old Labour leader's diary for March

parts.note: Michael Foot led the UK Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
a log is a diary or daily record

explanation.surface: A former party leader's private journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is the verb, to walk; the capital disguises it as the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To footslog is to march or trudge a long way on foot.

clue.text: With skill embraces woman deserving love

indicators.note: embraces puts the skill word around the woman's name

parts.note: able means with skill, competent
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A capable person hugs a lovable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is lovable, worthy of affection.

clue.text: Traveller's joy seeing father's to tolerate daughter

parts.note: the old man is slang for father
to bear is to tolerate

explanation.surface: Seeing Dad's tolerant of his daughter brings joy to a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traveller's joy' is a plant name, not a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man's beard is another name for wild clematis, also called traveller's joy.

clue.text: Couturier provides such an elegant sample

indicators.note: sample means only a portion of the phrase is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A fashion designer offers an elegant swatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco Chanel was the French fashion designer who founded the famous Paris house.

clue.text: Swimmer swears violently

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters of the word are thrown about

explanation.surface: A bather curses furiously.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: Personnel retained by one directing exciting film perhaps

indicators.note: retained by puts the personnel letters inside the steering word

parts.note: a tiller is the bar that steers a boat, so it directs
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Staff kept on by a film director make an exciting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a suspense story, often a film; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Good court official is well

parts.note: an usher is an official in a law court

explanation.surface: A kindly court attendant is in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is an oil well that spouts freely without pumping.

clue.text: Garment, a Roman one

parts.note: a tog is an informal word for a garment, as in togs for clothes

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing of the kind worn in ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer robe of Roman citizens, the classic Roman garment.

clue.text: Liberal award for division

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A Liberal honoured with a medal causes a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded section of an organ such as the brain or lung, a part or division.

clue.text: Have a large holding of Grammar School property

parts.note: on the stock market, to be long in a share is to hold a large amount of it, hoping its price rises

explanation.surface: Owning a big stake in a selective school's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be long in' is stock-market jargon for holding a large amount of a share.
explanation.definitionFit: Belongings are the things a person owns, their possessions.

clue.text: Information about lake valley

indicators.note: about puts the information word around the letter for lake

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Facts about a lake and its valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: A doctor in the Oval returned casual footwear

indicators.note: in puts the doctor pieces inside the turned shape word
returned means the shape word is read backwards

parts.note: an ellipse is an oval shape

explanation.surface: A medic came back to the Oval cricket ground in relaxed shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here it is just a shape; 'returned' turns ELLIPSE into ESPILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole, worn informally.
